questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria?

options.text: Accepting savings deposits from school students
Acting as banker to the government and issuer of the naira

questions.stem: A commercial bank receives a new deposit of ₦50,000 and the cash reserve ratio is 10 per cent. What is the maximum additional credit, in naira, that the banking system can create?
questions.explanation: The credit multiplier is 1/0.10 = 10, so maximum total deposits are ₦500,000. Additional credit is total deposits minus the original deposit: ₦500,000 − ₦50,000 = ₦450,000. Equivalently, ₦50,000 × (1 − 0.10)/0.10 = ₦450,000.

questions.stem: Treasury bills traded in Nigeria are instruments of the

options.text: capital market, because they finance long-term projects
money market, because they are short-term government securities

questions.explanation: Treasury bills are short-term government paper, typically 91, 182 or 364 days, used to cover temporary cash needs. That maturity puts them firmly in the money market. Shares and bonds of several years’ life belong on the capital market, including the NGX.

distractorRationale.a: Long-term project finance is raised with bonds and equities, not with T-bills
distractorRationale.c: Insurance companies may buy T-bills as assets, but the bills themselves are money-market instruments
distractorRationale.d: The parallel foreign-exchange market is a different market altogether

questions.stem: Open Market Operations by the CBN involve

options.text: the buying and selling of government securities to influence bank liquidity
the printing of extra naira notes for commercial banks on request
the allocation of foreign exchange only to oil companies
the fixing of prices of staple foods in the market

questions.explanation: When the CBN sells Treasury bills, banks pay with reserves and their ability to lend shrinks; when it buys, it credits the banks and liquidity rises. That is OMO — a monetary-policy tool, not a price-control or note-printing exercise.

distractorRationale.b: Note issue is a separate CBN function and is not how OMO works
distractorRationale.c: Foreign-exchange management is a different CBN duty, not the definition of OMO
distractorRationale.d: Food-price fixing would be a form of price control, which is not monetary policy

questions.stem: A company raising long-term funds by issuing ordinary shares on the NGX is using the

options.text: money market, because shares can be sold the next day
capital market, because equity is a long-term source of finance
commodity market, because the NGX trades only agricultural produce

questions.explanation: Ordinary shares are permanent capital: the company need never repay them. That long-term character places them on the capital market, of which the Nigerian Exchange is the main organised venue. The fact that an investor can resell a share tomorrow does not turn the original issue into short-term money-market finance.

distractorRationale.a: Secondary-market liquidity does not change the long-term nature of equity as a source of funds for the firm
distractorRationale.c: The NGX is a securities exchange, not a produce market such as a commodity board
distractorRationale.d: The discount window is a CBN facility for short-term bank liquidity, not a place to issue shares

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of commercial banks in the economy?

questions.stem: How do commercial banks create credit?

options.text: By holding all deposits in reserve
By lending out a portion of deposits while keeping a reserve
By investing all deposits in government bonds
By collecting interest on loans only

questions.explanation: Commercial banks create credit by lending out a portion of the deposits they receive while keeping a certain percentage in reserve, known as the cash reserve ratio. This process allows banks to effectively multiply the money supply in the economy, facilitating more loans and stimulating economic growth.

distractorRationale.a: Holding all deposits in reserve would prevent banks from lending and creating credit.
distractorRationale.c: Investing all deposits in government bonds would limit the availability of funds for lending.
distractorRationale.d: Collecting interest on loans is a result of lending, not a method of creating credit.
